properties.name: A reflow2 HTTP server told to stop finishes the requests it has, closes every open design cleanly, and only then exits
properties.statement:
On SIGTERM or SIGINT, a reflow2 server serving over HTTP (a single design, or a registry root):
- SHALL stop accepting new connections;
- SHALL let requests already in flight finish, within a bounded grace period that is configurable and shorter than a container's own stop timeout;
- SHALL close every open design store cleanly before exiting.
A deploy (docker stop, systemd stop, a Kubernetes rollout) therefore never cuts a write in half, and the next start opens stores that were shut down cleanly.

WHY, in @ajs's words (2026-09-27): "Yes, let's build the now items in reflow2". It was one of the research's "now" items: Meta's Shard Manager measured planned events about 1,000× more frequent than failures, so a clean handoff at deploy time matters more than crash recovery. flo2.io's engine upgrade on 2026-09-27 stopped and recreated the container twice in six minutes. Cloudflare's Durable Objects give in-flight requests up to 30 s on deploy.

NOT IN IT: moving a design to another machine, which is the placement-table step at scale.
